items.title: GitHub Contributions: Let users request improvements and share fixes
items.summary: Give users a public place to explain what they need and give contributors a clear way to offer improvements. Our team reviews submitted code before including accepted changes in an official Edge Studio release.
criteria: Public requests use approachable GitHub forms; non-developers do not need to write code.
Private feedback stays private and public links never copy submissions or diagnostic data automatically.
Contribution rights, triage/review ownership and branch/release expectations are documented before public launch.
A fork pull request can be checked and reviewed without private team credentials; accepted work follows normal releases.
Module Builder remains deferred and unchanged; source contributions and future installable modules can coexist.

items.title: GitHub Contributions: Help people build and test new capabilities
items.summary: Publish clear instructions and optional AI guidance that help people add hardware, devices and workflow behaviour to their own copy of Edge Studio. Prove that a new contributor can build, test and submit a complete improvement.
criteria: Clean local and fork-to-Pi source builds demonstrably run the contributor's changed code.
Public guides explain architecture and complete hardware/device/wizard/guide/workflow integration changes.
A portable AI contribution skill follows the same public guidance without internal OpenProject access or team secrets.
An independent contributor proves a physical integration and related workflow behaviour on a test Pi and submits it for normal human review.
The current security boundaries remain in force; no Module Builder runtime/package system is introduced.

items.title: Agree contribution rules and how public requests are handled
items.summary: Explain how people can ask for improvements or offer code, and how our team will respond and review it. Agree the rights and responsibilities before inviting public code contributions.
criteria: Provide CONTRIBUTING.md and concise triage/review guidance using existing conventions rather than a second ruleset.
Explain local forks, public issues, private feedback, private security reports, branch/PR targets and normal release expectations.
Document a small request-label/status process, duplicates and maintainer responsibilities without promising unagreed response times.
Obtain rights-holder agreement on project licensing and contribution terms before public launch; this ticket does not preselect a license.
Use existing #690 work; public users do not need internal OpenProject access.

items.title: Give users simple forms for public requests
items.summary: Let people report bugs or ask for hardware support, workflow features and other improvements through simple GitHub forms. Other users and contributors can browse these requests and help solve them.
criteria: Provide bug, device-support, workflow-request and general-improvement forms plus chooser guidance.
Ask plain-language problem/outcome questions, relevant app/device details and available testing help; do not require code.
Explain public visibility and GitHub-account requirements; redirect security concerns privately.
Use optional sanitized screenshots/excerpts; no automatic private feedback or log-archive attachments.
Validate required labels, schema and actual GitHub rendering and walkthrough usability.

items.title: Help contributors run their own version of Edge Studio
items.summary: Give contributors reliable steps to run Edge Studio locally and on a test Pi with their own changes. Check that they are really running their modified code rather than an unchanged official build.
criteria: Publish a clean-checkout quickstart using supported prerequisites, actual scripts and platform limitations.
Verify a harmless visible source change in local development and a fork build on a disposable test Pi, recording the source/commit.
Test/document APP_REPO_URL, APP_BRANCH and DEV_MODE/source-build behaviour without assuming a branch switch changes prebuilt images.
Explain development signing/update differences, data/helper-state preservation and return to official releases without weakening official defaults.
Require no private team credentials; fix only specific reproducibility blockers found by the trial.

items.title: Explain how Edge Studio works for contributors
items.summary: Provide a clear map of the app so contributors know where a change belongs. Explain how the screens, saved data, hardware services and workflows work together.
criteria: Publish a concise architecture guide and diagram with real, validated source links.
Cover frontend/backend/database/workflows/history, host agent/helpers, installer/Docker, updater and Minima/Integritas boundaries.
Explain hardware enablement versus configured devices, source roles, persistence/migrations, secrets and errors.
Describe current narrow hardware interfaces and opt-in behaviour; do not imply the deferred privileged extension runtime already exists.
Link existing public rules and ADRs without internal tools or machine-specific paths.

items.title: Show how to add hardware, devices and setup guides
items.summary: Show contributors the full set of changes needed to support a device, including hardware setup, saved settings and the screens and guides users see. Use a complete working example so important steps are not missed.
criteria: Publish a worked device recipe classifying readable/event/capture/output/helper roles and when to reuse an existing type.
Map current backend validation/runtime/helper/config and frontend template/form/alternate wizard/config/guide paths accurately.
Cover saved-device editing, visibility, prerequisites, repeatable setup, structured errors, credentials and existing hash/media behaviour.
Include safe starter workflows, focused tests and real hardware/environment verification with explicit limitations.
A complete integration includes backend, UI, setup guide and tests; current host boundaries remain unchanged.

items.title: Show how to add workflow steps and logic
items.summary: Explain how to add or extend a workflow step from its settings screen through to what it does when a workflow runs. Include examples and tests that preserve saved workflows and useful run history.
criteria: Publish a harmless worked workflow recipe explaining reuse versus new block/event behaviour.
Trace UI types/library/help/inspectors/summaries/canvas to backend validation/execution/policy/persistence using current paths.
Cover roles, configuration validation, events/listener lifetime, cancellation, errors and run/block history.
Preserve existing media/hash/proof relationships, budgets, saved-workflow compatibility and irreversible-action protections.
Document focused checks and Pi/external-service tests needed for the actual change; do not redesign the engine or add module contracts.

items.title: Link Edge Studio to public requests and contribution guides
items.summary: Help users find community requests and contribution instructions from the app. Keep the existing private feedback option clearly separate so users understand what will be public.
criteria: Provide clear browse-requests, public-request and contribution-guide actions in the smallest suitable existing app surface.
Reuse FeedbackModal/help/navigation patterns and #618 investigation; a new sidebar tab is not mandatory.
State that GitHub submissions are public and require an account.
Pass no private feedback text, metadata, secrets or diagnostics in outgoing links; do not build a feedback-to-issue bridge.
Verify real destinations, responsive usability and unchanged private feedback behaviour.

items.title: Review community changes and release accepted contributions
items.summary: Give contributors and reviewers a clear process for checking a proposed change, discussing improvements and deciding whether to accept it. Accepted changes reach other users through the normal Edge Studio release process.
criteria: Provide a PR template covering problem/change, related issue, affected surfaces, tests, hardware evidence, limitations and docs.
Document dev/main branch flow, reviewer/merge ownership, hardware evidence requirements and fork-update guidance.
Verify fork PR checks using existing workflows/approval policies without secrets or privileged execution of untrusted code.
Require the same quality/testing bar for AI-assisted changes; do not represent generated code as verified.
A real fork PR receives a recorded human decision and a normal release path; publishing a PR is not automatic acceptance or deployment.

items.title: Provide an AI skill that guides complete contributions
items.summary: Give contributors reusable instructions they can load into their own AI tools. The instructions help the AI understand Edge Studio, make a complete change, run checks and prepare a useful pull request.
criteria: Provide a discoverable public contribution skill with repository-local/manual installation, update and version-matching instructions.
Reuse current add-device-support/rules and public human guides; synchronize required agent-tool mirrors and avoid conflicting rulebooks.
Guide classification, affected-file discovery, code/docs/tests, honest check results, hardware limitations and PR preparation.
A clean contributor environment needs no private OpenProject, team Pi, credentials, hosted Module Builder or particular paid AI provider.
Validate actual guidance loading and a representative task in a supported harness; the human-only path remains usable.

items.title: Prove a new contributor can complete a real integration
items.summary: Ask someone outside the core team to follow the public guidance, add a real device and related workflow behaviour, test it on a Pi and submit the change. Use what they struggle with to improve the guides and AI skill.
criteria: An independent contributor follows a public request, forks/clones, makes a source change and builds the changed app on a test Pi with actual hardware.
Record source/app versions, environment, physical evidence, checks, assistance needed and corrected guide/skill gaps.
Submit and review the real PR through the normal process; acceptance is readiness for normal release, not a forced production merge.
A non-developer completes the request-form walkthrough; separately exercise AI guidance if the integration author used the human-only route.
No private team tools or deferred Module Builder are dependencies, and no private feedback is exposed.
